design_rationale:
STEP 0 -- asset ledger & claim. Task 1 of 2 (the final task) for membership_lifecycle. Task 0
claimed membership_ext_dues_waiver_medical_hold, membership_ext_enrollment_fee and
membership_ext_recurring_dues (all disjoint from this task's assets). This task claims the
difficulty's single workflow, membership_wf_past_due_cancellation_settlement, together with its
three embedded policies membership_ext_late_fee, membership_ext_reactivation_settlement and
membership_ext_early_termination_fee -- the whole remaining policy set, so all 6 extended policies
across the two tasks are now covered with pairwise-disjoint scopes.

Design thesis: Marcus volunteers only "I want to settle up and cancel" -- he never names the missed
late fee, the reactivation mechanics, or the fact that a cancellation can only be filed once the
contract is active again. Core scored parameter chain: charge_early_termination_fee's amount_usd
(root), which cannot be correctly reached (or reached at all, per the base cancellation-request
transition set) while the contract is past_due. Depth: surface goal "cancel and be done with it" ->
discover the contract is past_due -> discover the missed cycle's late fee was never assessed ->
assess it -> pay the full current balance to reactivate -> reactivate -> file notice -> assess the
early-termination fee now that notice exists and the contract is not past_due. Breadth: rolling
12-month late-fee escalation history, corporate wellness employer_pct/multi_location_pct/
wellness_reimbursement_pct/cap cross-category factors (multi_location_discount_pct=0 for Small
Business Partner throughout -- a real, untriggered branch on every one of the three policies), and
the prorated-by-remaining-term calculation for the termination fee itself.

Base-invariant card: membership_tier_dues_billing.dues_charge_requires_open_contract (state) --
allowed=[applied,active,frozen,past_due,cancel_pending]; membership_holdings.status='past_due' at
steps 6 (late_fee) and 14 (early_termination_fee, by then status='cancel_pending' after step 12) --
both in the allowed set. membership_corporate_bundling.corporate_discount_requires_active_enrollment
(state) -- corporate_wellness_enrollments[corp1].status='active', satisfied throughout.
membership_early_termination_fee.within_minimum_term (time) -- anchor=opened_date=2024-09-05,
duration=minimum_term_months=12 (Premier All-Access), relation=not_after, boundary=exclusive;
frozen_time=2025-01-05 is only 4 months after opened_date, well inside the window; boundary case: at
2025-09-05 the window closes (exclusive). membership_payment_application.no_duplicate_payment_posting
(dedup) -- no membership_payment_received row exists yet at frozen_time's exact moment for this
membership, so the new reactivation payment is not a duplicate. membership_past_due_closure and
membership_cancellation_notice do not govern any of this task's exact write subjects
(membership_dues_charge / membership_payment_received / membership_reactivated /
membership_cancellation_requested), since their own eligibility gates are scoped to
membership_closed only, which this task never writes.

Business-object card: target object = membership_holdings[memb1] for cust1. Correlation key =
membership_id. History rows: e1/p1 (Sep enrollment, settled), e2/p2 (Sep dues, settled), e3/p3 (Oct
dues, settled), e4+e5/p4 (Nov dues + an EARLIER, fully-settled late fee episode -- e5 is the "one
prior late_fee in the trailing 12 months" that escalates THIS episode's fee), e6 (Dec dues, UNPAID --
the current past_due trigger, dues_balance=64.99 exactly equals e6's amount since every earlier row
nets to zero). No other holding/customer is seeded.

Problem-tree card: root=membership_ext_early_termination_fee. Edge 1 (state_gate) ->
membership_ext_reactivation_settlement: gate=membership_holdings.status; condition "the member must
currently be in active or frozen standing rather than past_due, since a cancellation request may only
be filed from active or frozen status"; policy_source quoted verbatim from the root's own rule;
unresolved at frozen_time because initial_state.membership_holdings[memb1].status = 'past_due', not
active or frozen; resolved_by pay_reactivation_balance_4f725d24 (immediately followed by the
reactivate transition, the next step of the same procedure). Edge 2 (value_input, chained one hop
further) -> membership_ext_late_fee: gate=current_balance; condition "the current dues_balance must
reflect any late_fee charge already posted for the missed payment before the reactivation payment
amount is computed"; policy_source quoted verbatim from membership_ext_reactivation_settlement's own
rule; unresolved at frozen_time because dues_balance=64.99 reflects only the unpaid Dec recurring_dues
charge e6, with no late_fee row yet for this missed-payment episode (e5 is an earlier, already-settled
episode from November); resolved_by charge_late_fee_8963437d. Both edges are chained (A depends on B
depends on C), so no parallel-order ambiguity: the only legal order is
membership_ext_late_fee -> membership_ext_reactivation_settlement -> membership_ext_early_termination_fee.
no_user_hint: user_scenario never names the missed payment, the late fee, or the reactivation
mechanics -- Marcus states only that he wants to settle up and then cancel, and reacts only to what
the representative reports back. tools_do_not_block: none of charge_late_fee_8963437d,
pay_reactivation_balance_4f725d24, reactivate_membership_73e153df, file_cancellation_notice_df814962
or charge_early_termination_fee_74e8dbe7 read or check any of these facts before writing (see
task_tools.py: each looks up only the membership_holdings row to confirm it exists, then
unconditionally performs its one write) -- calling charge_early_termination_fee_74e8dbe7 while still
past_due, or before the late fee is reflected in dues_balance, would post a charge and a terminal
state that simply differs from gold.

Deletion sensitivity (Step 5 prerequisite-sensitivity run): skipping charge_late_fee_8963437d leaves
current_balance at 64.99 (instead of 81.87), dropping the reactivation payment result from 103.12 to
86.24 -- edge 2 is load-bearing (verified by check_compute.py's own value_input replay). Skipping
pay_reactivation_balance_4f725d24 (and the following reactivate transition) leaves
membership_holdings.status at past_due when charge_early_termination_fee_74e8dbe7 is called and the
cancellation-request table empty, since filing notice from past_due is not a modeled transition at
all -- the terminal membership_holdings.status and membership_cancellation_requests contents both
differ from gold -- edge 1 is load-bearing (state_gate; not machine-checkable by check_compute.py,
confirmed by this manual audit instead).

Standard solution / verification (also the handling-time recomputation, matching computations[] and
the gold arguments exactly): membership_ext_late_fee at step 6 -- base_late=P('late_fee_usd')=15.00
(Premier); prior_late_count=COUNT(charge_type=late_fee, within 12mo)=1 (row e5, 2024-11-10, within 12
months of 2025-01-05); escalated=15.00*1.5=22.50; corp_active=True; reimb_pct=
CPARAM('corp','wellness_reimbursement_pct')=25 (Small Business Partner); multi_loc_pct=
CPARAM('corp','multi_location_discount_pct')=0 (untriggered); reimb_cap=
CPARAM('corp','wellness_reimbursement_annual_cap_usd')=100.00; reduction=MN(RND(22.50*25/100,2),
100.00)=5.62; result=RND(22.50-5.62,2)=16.88. membership_ext_reactivation_settlement at step 8 (after
the late fee has landed) -- current_balance=F('dues_balance')=64.99+16.88=81.87; reactivation_fee=
P('reactivation_fee_usd')=25.00 (Premier); corp_active=True; employer_pct=
CPARAM('corp','employer_discount_pct')=15; multi_loc_pct=0; fee_reduction=RND(25.00*15/100,2)=3.75;
result=RND(max(81.87+25.00-3.75,81.87),2)=103.12. membership_ext_early_termination_fee at step 14
(after reactivation and notice) -- full_fee=P('early_termination_fee_usd')=179.00; term_months=
P('minimum_term_months')=12; months_elapsed=MONTHS('2024-09-05','2025-01-05')=4; months_remaining=
MX(12-4,0)=8; prorated=RND(179.00*8/12,2)=119.33; reimb_pct=25; multi_loc_pct=0; reimb_cap=100.00;
reduction=MN(RND(119.33*25/100,2),100.00)=29.83; result=RND(max(MN(119.33-29.83,179.00),0),2)=89.50.
This has been executed as plain Python (see the design-note computation trail above and re-run
against check_compute.py) and matches computations[].expected and the gold arguments exactly.

Zero-wait causal card (per workflow step): step0 (charge_late_fee, agent) -- prerequisite: the missed
Dec cycle's recurring_dues charge and the tier's late_fee_usd/escalation history are all
initial_state_preexisting (initial_state.membership_events, initial_state.membership_holdings);
zero_wait_proof: posting a late fee for an already-missed payment is an ordinary atomic ledger write,
nothing external need occur. step1 (pay_reactivation_balance, agent) -- prerequisite: the up-to-date
dues_balance is a prior_synchronous_tool_effect of step0 (the late fee charge just landed in this
same consultation); zero_wait_proof: the representative reads the now-current balance and the member
authorizes payment of that exact figure in this same call, no external clearing wait. step2
(reactivate_membership, agent) -- prerequisite: the reactivation payment is a
prior_synchronous_tool_effect of step1; zero_wait_proof: flipping status once the balance is paid is
an ordinary atomic status write. step3 (file_cancellation_notice, user) -- prerequisite: the
contract's active status is a prior_synchronous_tool_effect of step2, and the member's intent to
cancel is current_user_input (stated in this same call); zero_wait_proof: filing notice is an
ordinary atomic write the member performs themselves once the agent hands over the tool, no external
event required. step4 (charge_early_termination_fee, agent) -- prerequisite: the filed notice and the
non-past_due status are prior_synchronous_tool_effects of step3/step2; zero_wait_proof: assessing the
fee from the tier's own parameters and the corporate offset is an ordinary atomic ledger write,
nothing external need occur.

Draft recomputation from the visible context alone (masking compute/expected/GT): a rollout agent
reading only the published KB, the tool schemas and Marcus's own words would: verify identity; read
the membership holding (past_due, opened 2024-09-05) and its full event history (an unpaid Dec
recurring_dues charge, a settled Nov late-fee episode); notice the published rule for filing a
cancellation notice requires active or frozen standing, so past_due must first be resolved; read that
membership_ext_late_fee's own rule requires escalating on any PRIOR late_fee in the trailing 12
months (found: e5); post the late fee, then the reactivation payment (balance plus fee minus the
employer offset), then reactivate, then file notice, then assess the early-termination fee prorated
by the remaining term and reduced by the same employer's reimbursement, reading the linked corporate
wellness enrollment throughout. This agrees with gold.

Rework round 2 (policy-task audit response, revision 2 of this task file): closed two undeclared-override findings (audit findings 1-2 in 1.md) by adding a declared overwrite entry to each of membership_ext_late_fee (superseded_clause "on each recurring_dues charge" from membership_corporate_bundling, since that base rule scopes its comparable employer-funded reduction to recurring_dues only, and this policy extends the same class of benefit to a late_fee charge through a different corp parameter) and membership_ext_early_termination_fee (superseded_clause "the fee is waived entirely when relocation_termination_fee_waived applies to a documented relocation beyond relocation_radius_miles" from membership_early_termination_fee, since that base rule treats the amount as strictly binary -- full flat fee, or zero on documented relocation -- while this policy replaces that binary treatment with a continuous proration, and relocation is now handled as a separate full waiver outside this formula). Neither policy has any base_policy_ref whose own RULE TEXT (as opposed to the parameter_schema prose describing late_fee_usd/early_termination_fee_usd as a "flat fee") states a formula for these two quantities at all -- no cited base policy's rule mentions late_fee by name, and membership_early_termination_fee's own rule governs only eligibility timing plus the one waiver clause now declared above -- so the escalation (1.5x repeat-delinquency) and pro-rata (months-remaining/term) mechanisms themselves have no base RULE sentence to formally supersede via overwrite (Principle D's own test is base's RULE for the quantity, not its parameter_schema description or its params-level flat alias, which "remain valid and are still carried by base" independent of any override declaration). Both policies' rule text was rewritten to close this gap directly in prose instead: each now opens by stating plainly that no base policy rule supplies any formula for this charge's amount, that this policy is therefore the sole and exclusive determination of the billed amount, and exactly which single case (no escalation/no reimbursement; zero months elapsed/no reimbursement) numerically coincides with the bare tier parameter parameter_schema calls flat -- so an agent reading either policy's rule alone, without ever needing to fall back to the base parameter_schema line, is told unambiguously that the formula below is authoritative. Also fixed (audit finding 4/observation, and _difficulty.md finding 4): the membership_ext_early_termination_fee -> membership_ext_reactivation_settlement state_gate edge's effect field previously implied pay_reactivation_balance_4f725d24 itself flips membership_holdings.status; resolved_by is mechanically required to name the depended-on PROBLEM's own target_tool (prereq_utils.validate_declarations: resolved_by must equal that policy's target_tool when problem is a policy id), and reactivate_membership_73e153df is not itself a policy/problem node (it computes nothing -- its only argument is membership_id -- so it cannot be given a compute of its own without inventing a parameter that does not exist), so resolved_by correctly continues to name pay_reactivation_balance_4f725d24 as the reactivation-settlement PROBLEM's own canonical action. What was corrected is the effect wording itself, both here and in the mirrored prerequisite_closure edge below: it now states precisely that pay_reactivation_balance_4f725d24 pays the balance to zero, and that reactivate_membership_73e153df -- the workflow's own very next step, governed by order_rationale rather than by any policy's compute -- is what actually flips the status field, removing any implication that the named tool performs that flip itself. None of these changes alter any scored value, GT call, tool, owner, or write order; re-run against check_extended/replay_tasks/check_solvability/check_compute/check_grounding/check_cross_fire, all green (see worklog).
user_scenario: Marcus Chen calls in sounding matter-of-fact and a little tired of dealing with it. He says his membership has fallen behind on payments and he wants to get it squared away -- and once that's done, he's decided he wants to go ahead and cancel the membership altogether rather than keep paying for it. He'd like to know exactly what he owes to get current, and then he wants to give his notice to cancel right after. If asked to verify his identity, he gives his phone number as 2125550102 and, if a second detail is needed, his date of birth, 1988-11-02; if pressed further he can also give the last four digits of his photo ID, 7734, or say he's been a member since September 5th of 2024. He knows he's on the Premier All-Access plan and that he also gets some kind of discount through his employer, Redline Logistics, which has a corporate partnership with the club -- he doesn't know the percentage or how it's applied, and if asked just says 'that's through Redline Logistics, my employer, but you'd have to look up the details.' He does not know why his account fell behind, doesn't mention a late fee, and doesn't ask about it -- as far as he's concerned he just needs to be told the number to bring things current. If the representative explains that a missed-payment fee has to be added before the total is right, he just says 'Okay, whatever's actually owed, just add it in and tell me the total,' without asking why or disputing it. Once told the amount needed to bring the account current, he agrees to pay exactly that amount right away. Once the representative confirms the account is active again, he says 'Good, now let's cancel it' and, when handed the tool to submit his own cancellation notice, goes ahead and submits it for the date the representative gives him. He does not ask about a notice period or a final bill in advance, but once the representative tells him a final early-termination charge has been billed and states the amount, he says that's fine and thanks them for sorting everything out; he does not ask for anything further and does not request any document be sent.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping pay_reactivation_balance_4f725d24 (and the following reactivate transition) leaves membership_holdings.status at past_due when charge_early_termination_fee_74e8dbe7 is called, and leaves membership_cancellation_requests empty, since filing notice from past_due is not a modeled transition -- the terminal status field and the cancellation-request table both differ from gold.
Skipping charge_late_fee_8963437d leaves current_balance at 64.99 (instead of 81.87), dropping the reactivation payment result from 103.12 to 86.24.

prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: charge_late_fee_8963437d, pay_reactivation_balance_4f725d24, reactivate_membership_73e153df and file_cancellation_notice_df814962 each perform no read of the other's prior effect and no eligibility check at all before writing (see task_tools.py: each looks up only the membership_holdings row to confirm it exists, then unconditionally performs its one write); calling charge_early_termination_fee_74e8dbe7 or file_cancellation_notice_df814962 while status is still past_due would not error, it would simply write a terminal state that differs from gold.
